questions.q: Consider a circle $C$~which touches the $y -$~axis at~  \left(0, 6\right)$ and cuts off an intercept $6\sqrt{5}$~on the $x -$ axis. Then the radius of the circle $C$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have, a circle $C$~which touches the $y -$~axis at~ \left(0, 6\right)$ and cuts off an intercept $6\sqrt{5}$~on the $x -$ axis.

We know that, length of the~chord of the circle using perpendicular distance from the center is~$2\sqrt{r^{2} - d^{2}}$~where~$r$~is the radius of the circle and~$d$~is~the perpendicular distance from the center~to the chord.

From the given data, we have the following diagram

Hence,~length of the~chord of the circle~$⇒ 2\sqrt{r^{2} - d^{2}} = 6\sqrt{5}$

$⇒ \sqrt{r^{2} - d^{2}} = 3\sqrt{5}$

On squaring on both sides

$⇒ r^{2} - d^{2} = 45$

$⇒ d^{2} = r^{2} - 45$

Given that circle touches the~$y -$axis at~ \left(0, 6\right)$. Therefore,~$d = 6$.

$⇒ r^{2} = 45 - 36$

$r = \sqrt{36 + 45}$

$r = 9$.

questions.solution:
Since circle touches the x-axis at \left(3, 0\right),$ hence centre can be taken as \left(3, \alpha\right)$ and radius $= \left|\alpha\right|$
Since y-intercept is 8, by applying Pythagorean theorem
${3}^{2} + {4}^{2} = {\alpha}^{2} ⇒ \alpha = 5, - 5$
Hence two circles are possible
${\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 5\right)}^{2} = 25$ and ${\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(y + 5\right)}^{2} = 25 .$

questions.q: The sum of the squares of the lengths of the chords intercepted on the circle, $x^{2} + y^{2} = 16,$ by the lines, $x + y = n, n \in N,$ where $N$ is the set of all natural numbers is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The length of the perpendicular from centre& \left(0, 0\right)$ ~to the line $x + y = n$ is \left|\dfrac{0 + 0 - n}{{1}^{2} + I^{2}}\right| = \dfrac{n}{2}$

Length of intercept $= 2\sqrt{{4}^{2} - \left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)2} = \sqrt{64 - 2n^{2}}$

$⇒$ Possible values of $n$~are $1, 2, \ldots . 5$

$⇒$ Sum of the square of lengths of intercepts

$= \mathop{Σ}_{n = 1}^{5}\left(64 - 2n^{2}\right) = 64 \times 5 - 2\mathop{Σ}_{n = 1}^{5}n^{2}$

$= 320 - 2\mathop{Σ}_{n = 1}^{5}n^{2} = 320 - 110 = 210

$

questions.q: The locus of the centres of the circles, which touch the circle, $x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$ externally, also touch the $y$-axis and lie in the first quadrant, is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, the centre of the circle whose locus is to& be determined is& $P ( h, k )$~and~it touches $y$-axis in the first quadrant and we know that if~a circle touches the~$y$-axis, then~its radius is equal to the absolute value of the~$x$-coordinate of the centre.

Hence, the~radius of the circle is~$= h .$

Also, we know that if two circles touches externally, then the distance between their centres is equal to the sum of their radii.

And, the centre and radius of a circle~$x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}$~is~ \left(0, 0\right)$~and~$1$~respectively.

Now, since~the circle with centre~ \left(h, k\right)$~and radius~$h$~touches $x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$externally, then

$⇒ h + 1 = \sqrt{h^{2} + k^{2}}$

Squaring both the sides, we get

$⇒ h^{2} + 2h + 1 = h^{2} + k^{2}$

$⇒ k^{2} = 2h + 1$

Now, to get the locus, replace~ \left(h, k\right)$~by~\left(x, y\right),$~to get

$y^{2} = 2x + 1 .$

Hence, the required locus is~$y^{2} = 2x + 1$

$⇒ y = \sqrt{1 + 2x}, x \ge 0 .

$

questions.q: A rectangle is inscribed in a circle with a diameter lying along the line $3y = x + 7 .$ If the two adjacent vertices of the rectangle are  \left(- 8, 5\right)$ and \left(6, 5\right),$ then the area of the rectangle $($in sq. units$)& is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, the two adjacent vertices of the rectangle are& \left(- 8, 5\right)$~and~\left(6, 5\right),$~the~$y$-co-ordinates of both of these points is same this means they lie on the line~$y = 5,$~which is parallel to the~$x$-axis.

And, we know that the sides of a rectangle are perpendicular to each other, hence the other two sides passing through these vertices are parallel to~$y$-axis.

Also, we know that the equation of a line parallel~$y$-axis is~$x = k .$

Therefore, the equation of the sides of the rectangle passing through~ \left(- 8, 5\right)$~and~ \left(6, 5\right)$~are respectively~$x = - 8$~and $x = 6 .$

And, hence the other two vertices of the rectangle can be taken as~ \left(6, a\right)$~and~\left(- 8, b\right) .$

And since the other side is parallel to $x$-axis, hence~$a = b .$

Here, diagonal subtends right angle at the circumference of circle, so its mid-point is the same as centre of circle, which lies on the given diameter.

The mid-point of a line segment joining the points~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$~and~ \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$~is~\left(\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2}}{2}, \dfrac{{y}_{1} + {y}_{2}}{2}\right),$~hence, the mid-point of the diagonal of the rectangle is~ \left(\dfrac{- 8 + 6}{2}, \dfrac{a + 5}{2}\right) = \left(- 1, \dfrac{a + 5}{2}\right)$

This point lie on the diameter~$3y = x + 7$

So,~$\dfrac{3\left(a + 5\right)}{2} = - 1 + 7$
$⇒ a + 5 = \dfrac{2\left(6\right)}{3}$

$⇒ a = - 1$

Hence, the vertices are~ \left(- 8, 5\right), \left(6, 5\right), \left($6, - 1\right)$~and~\left(-$8, - 1\right) .$

The distance between the points~\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)~and~\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)~is~$\sqrt{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)2 + \left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)2}$

Thus, the length of sides are $6$ and $14$~units.

Hence, area $= l \timesb = 14 \times6 = 84$& sq. units

questions.q: If a circle of radius& $R$~passes through the origin~$O$~and intersects the coordinate axes at~$A$~and $B$, then the locus of the foot of perpendicular from~$O$~on~$AB$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since, circle passing through origin intersect the coordinate axes at $A \text{ and } B$, hence $AB$ must be diameter and~$AB = 2R$.

Now, let foot of the perpendicular from origin upon $AB$ be $P \left(h, k\right)$.

Slope of line~$OP = $\dfrac{k - 0}{h - 0} = \dfrac{k}{h}

Since, line~$AB ⊥ OP ⇒$~slope of~$AB = - $\dfrac{h}{k}

Thus, equation of line $AB$ is $y - k = $\dfrac{- h}{k} \left(x - h\right)$

For co-ordinates of $A$, put $y = 0 ⇒ 0 - k = $\dfrac{- h}{k} \left(x - h\right) ⇒ x = \dfrac{h^{2} + k^{2}}{h}⇒ A\left(\dfrac{h^{2} + k^{2}}{h},$0)$.

For co-ordinates of $B$, put~$x = 0 ⇒ y - k = $\dfrac{- h}{k} \left(0 - h\right) ⇒ y = $\dfrac{h^{2} + k^{2}}{k}$⇒ B\left(0, $\dfrac{h^{2} + k^{2}}{k}\right).

Now, given~$AB = 2R$

Applying distance formula,

$⇒ $\sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{h^{2} + k^{2}}{h} - 0\right)}^{2} + {\left(0 - \dfrac{h^{2} + k^{2}}{k}\right)}^{2}} =$2R$

$⇒ {\left(h^{2} + k^{2}\right)}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{h^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{k^{2}}) =$4R^{2} ⇒ {\left(h^{2} + k^{2}\right)}^{3} = 4R^{2}h^{2}k^{2}$

Hence, locus is ${\left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right)}^{3} = 4R^{2}x^{2}y^{2}$

$

Given,

$P \left({a}_{1}, {b}_{1}\right)$and $Q \left({a}_{2}, {b}_{2}\right)be two distinct points on a circle with center $C ( \sqrt{2}, \sqrt{3} ),$

And~$O$ be the origin and $OC$ be perpendicular to both $CP$ and $CQ$,

So,~$PCQ$~will be a straight line

Now on plotting the diagram we get,

So,~$OC = \sqrt{\left(\sqrt{2}\right)2 + \left(\sqrt{3}\right)2} = \sqrt{5}$

Now let~$CP = CQ = I$
Now by using area of triangle~$OCP = \dfrac{1}{2} \timesOC \timesI$~we get,

$\dfrac{35}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{5} \timesI⇒ I = \sqrt{7}$

And~$OP = OQ = \sqrt{OC^{2} + I^{2}} = \sqrt{12}$

So,~${a}_{1}^{2} + {b}_{1}^{2} + {a}_{2}^{2} + {b}_{2}^{2} = OP^{2} + OQ^{2} = 12 + 12 = 24$

$

questions.q: Let $PQ$ be a diameter of the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 9$. If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the lengths of the perpendiculars from $P$ and $Q$ on the straight line, $x + y = 2$ respectively, then the maximum value of $\alpha\beta$& is _______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
& Let $P ( 3cos\theta, 3sin\theta ) ∴ Q ( - 3cos\theta, - 3sin\theta )$
given line $x + y - 2 = 0$~$∴ \alpha = \dfrac{| 3cos\theta + 3sin\theta - 2 |}{2}$
$\beta = \dfrac{| - 3cos\theta - 3sin\theta - 2 |}{2}$
$∴ \alpha\beta = \left|\dfrac{( 3cos\theta + 3sin\theta - 2 ) \cdot ( 3cos\theta + 3sin\theta + 2 )}{2}\right| = \left|\dfrac{9 ( 1 + \sin 2\theta ) - 4}{2}\right|$
$∴$ maximum of~$\alpha\beta = 7$

questions.q: If the circles& $x^{2} + y^{2} + 6x + 8y + 16 = 0$~and~$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2\left(3 - \sqrt{3}\right)x + 2\left(4 - \sqrt{6}\right)y = k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6}$,~$k > 0$, touch internally at the point~$P \left(\alpha, \beta\right), then~ \left(\alpha + \sqrt{3}\right)2 + \left(\beta + \sqrt{6}\right)2$& is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The circle& $x^{2} + y^{2} + 6x + 8y + 16 = 0$~has centre~ \left(- 3, - 4\right)$~and radius~$\sqrt{9 + 16 - 16} = 3$~units.

The circle~$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2\left(3 - \sqrt{3}\right)x + 2\left(4 - \sqrt{6}\right)y =$~$k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6}, k > 0$~has centre~ \left(\sqrt{3} - 3, \sqrt{6} - 4\right)$~and radius~$\sqrt{\left(\sqrt{3} - 3\right)2 + \left(\sqrt{6} - 4\right)2 + k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{k + 34}$

Given that these two circles touch internally, so

distance between their centres$= \left|\text{difference of radii}\right|$

$\sqrt{3 + 6} = \left|\sqrt{k + 34} - 3\right|$

$⇒ \sqrt{k + 34} - 3 = \pm 3$

Here,~$k = 2$~is only possible value \left(∵ k > 0\right)$

Now the equation of common tangent to both the circles is given by~$2\sqrt{3}x + 2\sqrt{6}y + 16 + k + 6\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{6} = 0$

$∵ k = 2$~then equation becomes~

$x + \sqrt{2}y + 3\sqrt{3} + 3 + 4\sqrt{2} = 0 ⋯ \left(i\right)$

$∵ \left(\alpha, \beta\right)$~are foot of perpendicular from~ \left(-3, - 4\right)$~to this common tangent, then

$\dfrac{\alpha + 3}{1} = \dfrac{\beta + 4}{2} = \dfrac{- \left(- 3 - 4\sqrt{2} + 3 + 4\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{3}\right)}{1 + 2}$

$∴ \alpha +3 = - \sqrt{3} \text{ and } \dfrac{\beta + 4}{2} = - \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \left(\alpha + \sqrt{3}\right)2 = 9$~and~ \left(\beta + \sqrt{6}\right)2 = 16$

Hence,~ \left(\alpha + \sqrt{3}\right)$2 + \left(\beta + \sqrt{6}\right)$2 = 25$

questions.q: $Let the point&  \left(p, p + 1\right)$~lie inside the region~$E = \left\{\left(x, y\right): 3 - x \le y \le \sqrt{9 - x^{2}}, 0 \le x \le 3\right\} .$~If the set of all values of~$p$~is the interval~\left(a, b\right),$~then~$b^{2} + b - a^{2}$~is equal to~________ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The point& \left(p, p + 1\right)$~lie inside the region~$E = \left\{\left(x, y\right): 3 - x \le y \le \sqrt{9 - x^{2}}, 0 \le x \le 3\right\}$,

And~the set of all values of~$p$~is the interval~ \left(a, b\right),$~

Now by observation~\left(p, p + 1\right)$~lies on~$y - x = 1$,

Also point~ \left(p, p + 1\right)$~lies on~$x + y = 3$

So, solving~$y - x = 1$~and~$x + y = 3$~we get,~$P \left(1, 2\right)$

Again given point \left(p, p + 1\right)$~lies on $x^{2} + y^{2} = 9$

So, solving~$y - x = 1$~and~$x^{2} + y^{2} = 9$, we get

$x^{2} + ( 1 + x{)}^{2} = 9$

$⇒ 2x^{2} + 2x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + x - 4 = 0 . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 4 \cdot 4}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 1}{2}$

Hence,~$p \in \left($1, \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 1}{2}\right)$

Now on comparing with~$p \in \left(a, b\right)$~we get,

$⇒ a = 1, b^{2} + b = 4$~ ~[using \left($i\right)$]

Hence, the value of~$b^{2} + b - a^{2} = 4 - 1 = 3

$

The minimum distance between any two points ${P}_{1}$ and ${P}_{2}$ while considering point ${P}_{1}$ on one circle and point ${P}_{2}$ on the other circle for the given circles' equations

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 10x - 10y + 41 = 0$

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 24x - 10y + 160 = 0$& is ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& ${C}_{1} ( 5, 5 ) , {r}_{1} = 3$~and~${C}_{2} ( 12, 5 ) , {r}_{2} = 3$

${C}_{1}{C}_{2} = 7$

Now,~${C}_{1}{C}_{2} > {r}_{1} + {r}_{2}$

Thus,~\left({P}_{1}{P}_{2}\right)min = 7 - 6 = 1$
